maria.dev: Heads-up: after enabling the NF4 fast-path on canary, we saw a ~25% throughput drop and ~1.2GB GPU memory increase on a subset of hosts. Attaching a tiny log snippet below.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rolled at 2026-03-16T12:03Z by pipeline #canary-452
aj: Can you paste the perf trace or a flamegraph? Any obvious KV cache eviction correlation?

maria.dev: flamegraph: https://perf.internal/reports/263456 - short summary: kernel_scheduler time jumped, tiling-copy accounts for most of the extra time. p95 from 210ms -> 320ms on the canary nodes.

maria.dev: log snip:
```
[INF] model=redwood-nf4 kernel=tiling4 batch=8 seq=1024 p50=120ms p95=320ms gpu_mem=14.2GB evictions=12
[DBG] memcpy_async src=kv_cache dst=kernel_scratch size=1.2GB
[WRN] slab_fragments=47
```

tony_r: Sounds like tiling kernel is causing extra memcpy/alignment work for certain seq lengths. Try disabling tiling on the canary to see if it reverts. env KERNEL_TILING=0 ./rollout-canary.sh

aj: Also, capture nvprof/cuda-memstats while reproducing. If we see memcpy spikes coincident with scheduler churn that's a smoking gun.

sophia: FWIW I hit a similar symptom during fp4 calibration: quantized kernel emits an alignment copy when seq_len % 32 != 0 which fragments the KV slab. Quick pseudo-fix:
```
if (seq % 32 != 0) {
  pad = 32 - (seq % 32);
  // previous code -> per-request realloc
  // new: allocate from prealloc_slab[rounded_seq]
}
```

aj: Great note. Can you try reproducing with a script that drives batch=8, seq_len=1024 and monitor slab fragmentation? Which hosts reproduce? @maria.dev

maria.dev: Repro on gpu-rt-3 and gpu-rt-7. Repro script:
```
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://canary.api.local/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"redwood-nf4","inputs":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":512}' &
  sleep 0.2
done
```

tony_r: Also check host-level allocator stats and cudameminfo. Run with --trace-mem and --kernel-trace to collect timelines. If tiling is the culprit, we should see repeated small allocs in the runtime trace.

infra-bot: incident-bot: Created INF-6123: "NF4 canary: tiling kernel mem/copy surge" and attached canary logs. :rotating_light:

sophia: If padding is the root cause I can open a small PR to pre-allocate per-rounding-bucket slabs to avoid per-request realloc. That should remove the memcpy storms during mixed batch sizes.

aj: For immediate mitigation we'll throttle batching on canary to batch_size=4 and roll that out in 10m to see if p95/throughput stabilizes. I'll also kick off a bisect: tiling on/off and batch cap 4/8.

maria.dev: Thanks — running the throttled canary now and will post p95/gpu_mem after 30m.
